title: D-Skill: Distilling Teacher Knowledge through Agent Skills
primary_reason_zh: v1/v2 方法第 3 节逐段一致：根据已保存的 teacher/student 行为轨迹离线更新可复用技能，主路径不再次调用环境或评价；SkillOpt-backed 子实验另保留验证门。新版没有补成主方法的在线递归反馈闭环，维持原窄范围边界，issue #60 的主审核范围决定不能当外部故障。

changes.detail: Removed assertion that teacher skills are never visible throughout the entire pipeline; narrows statement to skill text not reaching analyst.

changes.check: Unchanged Table 1 includes chess 75.3%, so v2 conclusion aligns with table; current v1 wording must not silently be overwritten.

changes.detail: Removed claim that agent never receives correctness feedback; correct move advancing/incorrect ending remains environment behavior, no new evaluator is added to main offline skill construction.

changes.new: popularity >70, >200 plays, deviation <=85; 50 puzzles per 400-point band from 400 to 2000
changes.check: Evaluation/distillation counts stay 200/100 and tables unchanged. Changed collection specification should be explicit if v2 adopted.
Changes cap meaning; do not retain the v1 total-cap claim after adoption.

numeric_check: Direct readback of all five changed text blocks and unchanged result tables; no experimental rerun or recomputation.

evidence.quote: Once the trajectories have been collected, D-Skill operates fully offline: neither \pi_{S} nor \pi_{T} is invoked again, and skill construction requires no further environment access, ground-truth labels, rewards, or evaluation feedback.
The complete lesson pool is shuffled and partitioned into k chunks, which are processed sequentially to update the skill document.
All downstream stages, including merging, ranking, and validation gating, remain unchanged.
Each trace is truncated to its first 10,000 and last 35,000 characters
